expectations.evidence: The high-volume detector fires only when volume is below baseline in both a short window (about 15–60 minutes) and a long window (hours to a day). It compares against the same hour-of-week over 2–4 weeks. The low-volume detector fires only when the gap exceeds the learned p99 inter-arrival gap by a margin. It also gives examples: 'A nightly sync that has missed two nights is silent. A 3-calls/hour integration with a 40-minute gap is not.' So one quiet short interval cannot fire the alert alone. expectations.text: Uses a long enough comparison window that a single quiet interval does not fire the signal
expectations.evidence: The silence window is sized per flow at T ≈ 9/λ, so a normal gap has only about a 1e-4 chance of firing (about 4.5 h for a 2/hr partner). A 15-minute floor keeps jitter from paging. The partial-collapse detector needs volume below 20% of baseline for 3 consecutive windows, and the baseline comes from the trailing 4 weeks by hour-of-week. Not a full 5, because the gap detector still fires once a single window is exceeded. It relies on window sizing alone and does not require several quiet windows in a row.
